summary: Quarterly QBR with Argentum Bank covering usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap for Dedicated/Private pilot. Customer is seeing steady growth in token usage, rising costs from long-context document processing, and wants to validate Dedicated capacity and VPC options for data residency and lower latency. transcript:
Header: Recorded at 2026-07-21T15:00:00Z | Duration 42m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Liam O'Connor, Priya Nambiar (Redwood); Carlos Mendez, Sasha Ivanov, Renee Park, Avery Cole, Jordan Lee (Argentum)

00:00 Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we'll do a quick Q2 health check for the Redwood deployment at Argentum. I know we had some SLO hits in May so we'll cover reliability first and then usage and costs, and then roadmap. Carlos, you wanna kick us off with a quick update on how things are looking on your side?

00:18 Carlos Mendez: Yeah thanks Maya, uh overall things are good. We've ramped more team workflows into the document summarization pipelines, so token volume is up like 38% quarter-over-quarter, some days a high spike during month end. We did see the incident on May 14 - the drop in throughput when the KV cache warmed up - that cost us a few retries.

00:37 Liam O'Connor: Right I dug into that, the KV cache policy was default TTL at the time and the continuous batching queue hit a small starvation pattern when a burst of 12 concurrent long-context requests came in. We pushed a config patch which helped; still, the warm-up caused a couple of 500s for about four minutes.

00:55 Sasha Ivanov: Just to add, we saw elevated p95 latency, from our internal metrics, went from ~220ms to 480ms during the event. Our SREs had to increase the autoscale threshold as a temporary mitigation.

01:12 Maya Chen: Thanks Sasha. Quick question - are the retry counts driving up cost materially, or more of an availability annoyance?

01:20 Jordan Lee: It's a bit of both; retries plus longer context windows for compliance docs are increasing token spend. We're seeing more tail latency retries hitting additional token billing.

01:31 Priya Nambiar: On the Redwood side we flagged a few optimizations - prefix caching and batching tweaks - that reduce per-token compute impact. Liam, can you summarize the recommended config?

01:42 Liam O'Connor: Sure. We recommend enabling aggressive prefix/KV caching for the doc-summarization route, lower the initial batch timeout to 4ms for latency-sensitive traffic, and for longer context jobs use a dedicated job pool with quantized model profile to save cost. That combination reduced tokens-per-call cost in the benchmark we ran by roughly 18%.

02:03 Carlos Mendez: That's promising. For Dedicated - do you have a ballpark for what the unit economics look like compared to hosted per-token today?

02:12 Maya Chen: Yes, high level - Dedicated with reserved capacity targets a 30-45% reduction versus current hosted at your present utilization, but it depends on utilization and model mix. We'll send a tailored pricing sheet after this call.

02:26 Renee Park: Procurement will need the contract redline and SOC2/ISO docs. We already have the security questionnaire partially filled; can you confirm KMS and audit log retention options?

02:37 Priya Nambiar: Absolutely. We support customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated, and audit logs with configurable retention - can export to your SIEM. We'll upload the SOC2 Type II and ISO certs to the secure link after this meeting.

02:51 Avery Cole: A couple of SRE questions - for VPC/private deployment, what's the expectation for on-prem latency and the network egress? Also what about hardware footprint recommendations for a 10k rps equivalent in inference workload?

03:05 Liam O'Connor: For VPC, network latency typically adds 5-15ms depending on colo. For on-prem, hardware sizing depends on model family and quantization; for your 10k rps of short-chat style calls you could start with 4x H100-equivalent nodes with autoscale policies, but for long-context doc processing we'd recommend more memory and KV cache capacity. We'll put together a sizing worksheet.

03:30 Carlos Mendez: Great. Also, are there any known regressions with the latest quantized variants? We saw a minor quality delta on named entity extraction last month.

03:40 Liam O'Connor: Good call out. We observed a small NER delta in one of the 3-bit quant profiles. Our quality team flagged it; the workaround is to use the 4-bit profile for the NER-heavy pipeline or run a small ensemble with the higher-precision fallback. We'll include eval artifacts in the follow-up.

03:58 Maya Chen: Ok let's talk timeline - Carlos said you'd like to pilot Dedicated or Private in Q3, what's the pilot success criteria?

04:06 Carlos Mendez: Success for us is: sub-250ms p95 on short requests, less than 10% cost increase for long-context jobs vs current baseline, zero production data retention beyond session retention policy, and passing the security checklist. Also we want a reproducible benchmark that shows the unit cost improvement.

04:25 Priya Nambiar: Noted. We'll work on a benchmark plan aligned to those criteria. Liam will run a 2k token spike test simulating month-end, and we can run before/after caching and quantization profiles.

04:38 Jordan Lee: On observability - can you provide per-route token cost breakdown and traced requests for the pilot? That would help us attribute cost to features.

04:46 Maya Chen: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-route cost and latency, and we can add tracing hooks for the pilot routes. We'll provide a dashboard template.

04:55 Renee Park: On procurement, we need the sample PO wording and terms for Dedicated reserved capacity and also cancellation terms for pilot.

05:02 Maya Chen: I'll include a sample contract and term sheet. High level, pilots are month-to-month with the option to convert to a committed contract; specifics we'll include in the redline.

05:12 Carlos Mendez: One more thing - data residency. Some of our customers in EMEA require EU-only processing.

05:18 Priya Nambiar: We can do region pinning for Hosted, and Private can be deployed in your EU region. For Dedicated we have reserved pools in eu-west-1; we'll document the options.

05:28 Liam O'Connor: Quick follow-up on the incident root cause - it was a cache warm-up + batching starvation; permanent mitigation is to allocate a small warm pool and pre-warm KV for scheduled month-end jobs.

05:40 Carlos Mendez: That pre-warm approach sounds good. Could you also run a short runbook for our on-call team?

05:46 Liam O'Connor: Yep, we'll send a runbook with playbook steps and Grafana queries.

05:52 Maya Chen: Ok let's recap real quick - action items: pricing and contract, latency benchmark, schedule private deployment demo, provide SOC2/ISO and KMS details, and sizing worksheet + runbook. Anything else?

06:06 Carlos Mendez: No, that covers it. Appreciate the help and we'll aim to finalize pilot criteria by Jul 28.

06:12 Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up via the CRM and send the board items today. Bye.

Transcript notes: occasional transcription errors for proper nouns and model names; speakers occasionally overlap. Links shared: pricing sheet (link), SOC2 cert (link), benchmark spreadsheet (link).
